## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Suí translation by [闍那崛多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%97%8D%E9%82%A3%E5%B4%9B%E5%A4%9A) Jñānagupta (523–600), the **Suí re-translation** of the Indic original first rendered as [KR6j0574](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0574) *Jīngāng shàngwèi tuóluóní jīng* (T1344) by [佛陀扇多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E6%89%87%E5%A4%9A) Buddhaśānta in the Northern Wèi. The colophon reads "隋三藏法師闍那崛多譯". The Taishō editors mark the parallel — "[No. 1344]". Title-difference: T1344 reads 金剛上味 (*vajra-supreme-taste*), T1345 reads 金剛場 (*vajra-place* / *vajra-maṇḍala*); both Indic readings are plausible — Jñānagupta either had a manuscript with a different titling, or chose a deliberately divergent Chinese gloss.

**Abstract**

The frame and narrative arc are essentially the same as [KR6j0574](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0574): the Buddha at the Gold-Cave (*jīnkū* 金窟) at the *Miàosè* 妙色 settlement of the Snow-Mountain; alms-round; entry into the *yīqièfǎ píngděngxiāng sānmèi* 一切法平等相三昧 ("samādhi of the equal-mark of all dharmas"); the bhikṣus and gods cannot perceive the Buddha; they search; on emerging he pronounces the *Vajra-place* dhāraṇī. Jñānagupta's translation idiom is more closely calqued on Indic syntax than Buddhaśānta's; his transcription of the dhāraṇī uses the standard double-syllable phonetic markers.

The text-history situates the work in Jñānagupta's Suí phase, between his return to Cháng'ān in 581 and his death in 600. Nanjio N0428. The 大→聖 edition-marker indicates that the Shōgozō (聖語藏) collection at Tōdai-ji preserves a witness; the Shōgozō *kanchi* tradition has been important for early-Suí textual history.
